source.title: A Model of Double Descent for High-dimensional Binary Linear Classification
source.authors: Ze-Yu Deng; A. Kammoun; Christos Thrampoulidis

record.tranche_reason: Tests double descent in a new setting: high-dimensional binary linear classification with feature count varied, rather than deep networks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own test-risk curves as model size varies and its own test-risk comparisons across training-set sizes. Epoch-wise results are mentioned only as prior work and a possible future direction; they are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The paper derives and simulates test-risk curves for gradient descent on logistic loss in binary linear classification. It varies model size p through κ=p/n and sample size n. This bears on V4 (a non-deep model class) and V3 (more data hurting), in a setting different from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two corrections. First, the authors also prove a sharp phase transition: data are separable iff κ>κ⋆ with κ⋆<1/2, and GD matches ML below κ⋆ and SVM above it. The risk cusp sits at κ⋆, with a second descent after it. Second, dependence on the loss function comes from combining their results with the companion paper [KT20], not from this paper alone. Larger n can hurt at some model sizes under polynomial feature selection.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes high-dimensional binary linear classifiers using feature selection and asymptotic theory, with simulations of gradient descent on logistic loss; the motivating results concern larger deep networks and more data.
record.method_sensitivity: The curves and their minima depend on the data model, signal strength, feature-selection rule, training-set size, and loss. In the overparameterized regime, the risk can decrease monotonically or have a further U-shape depending on feature selection.

fits_no_version.finding: The asymptotic normalized max-margin √κ q⋆ decreases monotonically with κ. It therefore fails to predict the U-shape of the overparameterized risk curve (Fig 3 right).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin-based complexity measures do not track the shape of the double-descent risk curve in the interpolating regime.

record.peer_reviewed: Information and Inference: A Journal of the IMA
record.problems: Most risk values are shown only in figures without tabulated numbers or uncertainty estimates. The sample-size comparison does not establish that its example is near the interpolation threshold. Epoch-wise behavior is not measured.

untested.parts: Only linear classifiers are studied; there are no deep networks.
GD is run to convergence, so there is no epoch-wise test-error curve. Epoch-wise double descent is named only as future work.
Only binary linear classifiers with isotropic Gaussian features and logistic loss are covered, not a broad range of model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak location across axes.
There is no label-noise sweep and no regularization; multiple peaks are not studied.
Complexity is not re-expressed as an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Location of the global minimum. It lies beyond κ⋆ for linear feature selection at all SNRs, but can fall below κ⋆ for polynomial selection with γ=5. This is relevant to whether the second descent beats the classical optimum.
The interpolation threshold shifts right as n grows, under both feature-selection models.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this paper, so verdicts apply. Figure 6 training sizes are d/3, 2d/3 and d; the extraction rendered them as '13 d' and '32 d'. The overparameterized-regime U-shape under polynomial selection is a second U, not a second peak, so it is not counted as V6 multiple descent. Most evidence is figure-only, with no tabulated numbers; the only explicit values are Rbest and R at κ=0.05 in footnote 1.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses binary linear classifiers, not deep networks.
No test-error sweep over training epochs is reported.
The paper varies training-set size and reports a case where more data raises error, but does not establish that the illustrated model size is near the interpolation threshold.
Tests double descent for binary linear classifiers, not across a broad range of model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations across axes.
Does not test label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or disappearance of peaks under optimally tuned regularization.
Does not re-express complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that yields an ordinary U-shaped curve.

relationships.reason: In every plotted case risk peaks at the separability threshold κ⋆ and descends again beyond it. Simulations match theory in Figs 1, 4 and 5 (R1–R15).
relationships.display_finding: Risk peaked at the separability threshold κ⋆ and declined beyond it in every plotted setting, with simulations matching theory.
